task_contract.name: persistent_keyed_memory_neurons
task_contract.identity_rule: Each memory neuron has a stable key identity 0..7 across examples; one separate readout neuron receives a query key. Node identities are not token positions.
task_contract.data: Independent random values and queries; targets are values at the queried stable key, or the sum at the queried key and its cyclic successor. No edge labels are provided to training.

decision_rules.quality_effect: A task quality gain is supported only when graph test MSE improves over both controls by at least 20% in relative terms and the paired-seed 95% confidence interval of the relative delta excludes zero in the favorable direction.
decision_rules.interpretation: Failure to meet a threshold is an honest negative or inconclusive result; thresholds are evaluation rules, not training objectives.

cost_alignment.matching_rule: nearest integer hidden width; report actual ratios; linear MAC proxy excludes scatter/reduction, nonlinear, optimizer and memory costs

limitations: Two synthetic keyed-memory tasks do not establish broad neuron capabilities or natural-language benefit.

Stable identities are exercised across examples; remap_node_ids supports in-experiment reorder, addition and deletion while preserving surviving links. Saving identity registries across independent training runs remains caller-owned.
The policy is trained end-to-end through differentiable expected edge weights, then evaluated as discrete mutations at the fixed threshold.
The MLP controls match parameter count or a linear-MAC proxy separately; neither match captures scatter, nonlinear, optimizer or memory costs.
MPS and host memory are sampled every 2 ms and may miss shorter peaks; allocator counters are not exact per-model peak memory.
The scale sweep is a synthetic microbenchmark, not a production throughput guarantee.
